behavior.compaction: the pending element is removed by shifting the tail left: memmove over the remaining bytes when more than 16 bytes remain, a single 16-byte copy when 16 or fewer remain, skipped when the element is already last; vector end moves down by 16; the loop re-examines the same slot
behavior.completion: when the current slot reaches the vector end, the result is reset to 0, mutex A is unlocked, and 0 is returned
behavior.deletion: target freed with operator delete, size 0x18; element_count decremented by 1
behavior.empty_vector: begin == end returns 0 with only mutex A locked and unlocked
behavior.guard: found node value < element floor (unsigned) bails with the element key, removing nothing for that element
behavior.lock_order: mutex A, then mutex B per element; unlock order on bail is B then A; on a completed element B is unlocked before compaction, then re-locked for the next element
behavior.lookup_when_count_nonzero: bucket = key mod bucket_count; walk from the bucket predecessor's next, comparing keys while each subsequent node's key hashes to the same bucket; null or a different bucket bails with the element key
behavior.lookup_when_count_zero: linear walk from before_begin_next, comparing node +0x08 against the element key; a null step bails with the element key
behavior.removal_first_in_bucket: predecessor's next becomes the target's next; if the target's next hashes to a different bucket, that bucket's entry becomes the predecessor, and if the old bucket's entry was the sentinel, before_begin_next becomes the target's next, and the old bucket's entry is cleared to 0 (the target was its sole node)
behavior.removal_not_first_in_bucket: predecessor's next becomes the target's next; if the target's next hashes to a different bucket, that bucket's entry becomes the predecessor
behavior.throws: a nonzero pthread_mutex_lock result on mutex A or mutex B throws system_error; the landing stub at 0x5160777 moves the exception object to rbx and jumps to the cleanup at 0x516054e, which unlocks mutex A and resumes unwinding (LSDA mapping not claimed)

buckets.entry_meaning: predecessor node of the bucket's first node, the before-begin sentinel address (+0x50 field address) when the bucket's first node is the chain head, or 0 for an empty bucket
buckets.segment_rule: nodes of one bucket are contiguous in the chain; a walk stops at the first node whose key hashes to a different bucket

caller_census_method: full .text e8/e9 scan plus whole-file qword scan: exactly 3 direct calls, no tail jumps, no qword references

callers.role: twin wrapper: getter result in r12, sweep over the r8 struct, then the min-combination described in the README
twin wrapper, same shape with a different getter
passes a struct field at +0x1698 as the sweep struct; the enclosing routine is 2599 bytes and is census only

outer_layout.before_begin_next: +0x50 (first hash node, or 0; also the sentinel address used as a bucket predecessor value)
outer_layout.mutex_b: +0x78 (locked per element, unlocked after each element's hash removal)
outer_layout.table_fields_60_68_70: +0x60/+0x68/+0x70 (never read by this window; not claimed)
outer_layout.vector_capacity: +0x10 (never read by this window; not claimed)

pending_element.floor: +0x08 (removal requires hash node +0x10 >= this value, unsigned)
pending_element.key: +0x00 (compared against hash node +0x08; returned on bail)

preconditions_observed: on the bucket path, bucket_count is nonzero (the window divides by it)
on the bucket path, the bucket predecessor's next is a live node in a consistent table (the window reads its key without a null check)
the removal walk assumes the found node is reachable from its bucket predecessor (no null check in that walk)
shape_note: The bucket-predecessor and before-begin sentinel fixups in the removal match the standard library unordered-container erase shape; whether this window is first-party code or an inlined library routine is left to the maintainer. The sweep itself (pending vector, floor guard, mutex protocol, compaction, bail-with-first-key return) is the behavior pinned here, not the library shape alone.
unknowns: the semantic types of the pending key, floor, and hash node value fields (recorded neutrally as key/floor/value; no type is claimed)
the meaning of the outer +0x60/+0x68/+0x70 fields and the vector capacity slot (never read here)
what the twin wrappers' getters and second calls compute (census only; only their min-combination with the sweep result is pinned)

window.returns: 0 when the pending vector is fully swept; otherwise the first element key that could not be erased
